solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pompous page by posh female, bored

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so posh gives U
someone bored is fed up

explanation.surface: A snooty pageboy beside a bored upper-class lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conceited and self-important is said to be inflated, swollen with vanity.

clue.text: Overturn winning goal

parts.note: a side that is winning is up
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A late winning goal turns a match on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over is to turn it on its end, a straight synonym.

clue.text: To begin with, English novelist's describing craft

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so these words go around the next piece

parts.note: E. M. Forster was an English novelist, author of A Passage to India
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: An opening remark about how Forster's writing portrays his craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean 'as the first point', an idiom borrowed from the first course of a meal.

clue.text: A leader, inaccurate about western US state

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece
inaccurate suggests the letters are set down wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political leader gets facts wrong concerning a western American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurate' rearranges A LEADER to DELAARE, and 'about' wraps that around W.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the fifty states, the first to ratify the US Constitution.

clue.text: Article used by writer to make a point

definitions.text: Article used by writer to make a point

parts.words: Article used by writer to make a point
parts.note: reads like an essay arguing a case, but the object literally gives a pencil a sharp tip

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in which a columnist argues a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The device sharpens a pencil, giving the writing tool its point; article means object, not essay.

clue.text: Flash Gordon's head hairs curled

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
curled hairs are twisted round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The comic-strip hero Flash Gordon shown with his hair curled.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash looks like the hero's first name, but it is the definition, an adjective meaning showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash as an adjective means showy and vulgar, which is what gaudy, loud things are.

clue.text: Game actress, Mae, in comedy film

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game
Mae West was a Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: Mae West, ever game, stars in a comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1940 Marx Brothers comedy set in the Wild West.

clue.text: Sharply criticise a type of popular music

definitions.meaning: to rebuke someone, as in a sharp knock on the knuckles
the rhythmic spoken genre of hip-hop

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a sharp reprimand and the spoken-rhythm genre born in 1970s New York.

clue.text: The conventional postal service in Manila is bad, close to awful

indicators.note: letters that are bad are spoiled and must be put right by rearranging
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that the post in the Philippine capital is nearly dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges MANILA IS to SNAILMAI; 'close to' adds L from awful.
explanation.definitionFit: The jocular name for letters sent by post, slow compared with email.

clue.text: Cherished touching lake bird

parts.note: a pet is a cherished favourite
re means concerning or touching on
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A beloved bird seen at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of the open ocean, often seen skimming the waves.

clue.text: Latest on summit in the language of politicians, perhaps

parts.note: the latest is the news
a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: Fresh reports from the top of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's term for propagandist double-talk is often applied to evasive political jargon.

clue.text: Course over? Correct

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a course or trend, as in the tide of events

explanation.surface: Asking whether a course has ended, then being told it is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct text is to revise it for publication.

clue.text: With new firm in Kent town

indicators.note: new signals that the preceding word is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: stable means steady, firm

explanation.surface: A new company setting up in a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges WITH to WHIT. Kent is a county in south-east England; this is its seaside town famous for oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitstable is a harbour town on the north Kent coast.

clue.text: That memento, lost now

indicators.note: something lost is astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A keepsake has gone missing just now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at present, currently, a straight idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: French city map on centre of dresser

parts.note: a chart is a map
re means on, concerning

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here the central letter of dresser

explanation.surface: A map of a French city laid out on a sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a cathedral city south-west of Paris.

clue.text: What chorus girls did, providing great thrills

definitions.meaning: chorus-line dancers famously fling a leg up high
slang for intense excitement or fun

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the dancers' leg-flinging move and slang for excitement, as in getting a buzz.

clue.text: Adult feeding toddler perfectly

indicators.note: a piece feeding another is put into it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up spoons food to a little child with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exactly, to the last detail, as fitting someone just right.

clue.text: One who enjoys eating, guy tucking into fruit

indicators.note: one piece tucking into another goes inside it

parts.note: a gourd is a fruit, such as a pumpkin
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A man tucking into fruit, the picture of a happy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton or hearty eater who loves food in quantity.

clue.text: Giant in fairy tale therefore returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale giant, and so came back.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating monster of folk tales, like the one in Jack and the Beanstalk.

clue.text: Notably meat in a bolognese?

indicators.note: in places the meat inside the other letters

parts.note: bol is short for bolognese, as in spag bol
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A question about what meat goes into a bolognese sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that BOL, known from 'spag bol', is a loose abbreviation for bolognese.
explanation.definitionFit: Notably and the phrase both mean chiefly, more than anything else.

clue.text: Quiet lift gets approval

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to raise is to lift

explanation.surface: A silent elevator wins people's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is expressed approval or commendation.

clue.text: Tool for removing ice on broadcaster's building

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the tool follows the broadcaster

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster; the 's is read as 'has'
a scraper clears frost from a windscreen

explanation.surface: An ice scraper on a television company's premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall city tower block, a type of building.

clue.text: Sign of ladies losing weight

indicators.note: losing means a piece is dropped from the word

parts.note: ladies are women

explanation.surface: A sign that women are shedding pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Deer curiously circling one duck

indicators.note: circling means going round the next piece
curiously signals the letters appear in an odd order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A deer oddly circles round a single duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges DEER to EDER, and 'circling' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Venomous creature in house? Any number!

parts.note: Scorpio is one of the twelve astrological houses or signs
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A poisonous creature lurking in a home, perhaps several of them.
explanation.walkthrough: House here is the astrological sense, a sign of the zodiac, not a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: This arachnid stings with a poisonous tail.

clue.text: Gem cut for fabulous bird

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: rock is slang for a gem, especially a diamond

explanation.surface: A jewel cut into the shape of a mythical bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights; fabulous means legendary here.

clue.text: Old article about knight's schedule

indicators.note: about means going round the next piece

parts.note: aged means old
N is the chess notation for knight; the 's is read as 'has'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ancient item recording a knight's timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting, a programme of business.

clue.text: Mind seeing short film by head of Ealing

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end

parts.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mind drawn to a short film from Ealing Studios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last O of PSYCHO. Ealing Studios in London made classic British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or spirit, the mind.

clue.text: Bird reportedly studied by celebrity twitcher originally

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: studied means read, past tense, said like the colour
a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter

explanation.surface: A bird watched closely by a famous birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A twitcher is British slang for a keen birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird with a rust-red tail.
